subject: Commit ladder & MAP: VPC pilot acceptance, platform fee amortization
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@acmecorp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-11-11T09:22:00-05:00
Subject: Commit ladder & MAP for VPC pilot

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to formalize the evaluation plan so Procurement and Engineering can sign off. Attached is our internal evaluation checklist (Acme-Eval-Requirements.xlsx). High level asks from our side:

- A 90-day VPC pilot with an evaluation gate at 30/60 days (performance & security).
- A commercial ladder (commit percentages at pilot -> POC -> GA) tied to discounts; we need the math for TCO modeling.
- Clarity on the platform fee for Private/VPC: can it be amortized or credited against usage during ramp?
- A short SOW and an MSA redline to start procurement review.

Can you draft a mutual action plan (MAP) that maps milestones to commercial triggers? Procurement would like a close target of end of November to hit a December pilot start.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

—
Maya Rao
Head of Cloud Engineering, Acme Corporation
maya@acmecorp.com

Attachments: Acme-Eval-Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T11:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Commit ladder & MAP for VPC pilot

Maya — thanks for the checklist and the clear timetable. I've put together a draft MAP (MAP-railmap-v2.pdf) that ties the evaluation gates to a staggered commit ladder. Key points in the draft:

1) Pilot (0-30 days): Proof-of-concept in your VPC with performance baseline collection. If baseline meets the 99th percentile latency SLO in our shared test harness, we move to

2) POE (31-60 days): Security + SOC2 evidence review complete and throughput verification. Successful POE triggers a 30% committed capacity for 3 months at a preferred unit price.

3) GA ramp (61-90 days): If performance and security gates pass, a 12-month staircase commit is available with step discounts at 25/50/75/100% ramp milestones.

Platform fee proposal (initial): waive platform fee for the first 8 weeks of pilot. If Acme signs the 12-month staircase commit by the GA ramp gate, we amortize platform fee over the committed period and provide a credit equal to one month of platform fee after hitting 50% of committed usage within the first 3 months.

I've attached the MAP and an outline of commercial triggers. This is intentionally prescriptive to accelerate Procurement review — we can relax language where needed.

Proposed next step: I can convert the MAP into a short SOW and generate a draft MSA redline for your Procurement. Are you able to accept a DocuSign route if the commercial terms land this week?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
sofia@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: MAP-railmap-v2.pdf (diagram, 125KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@acmecorp.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:32:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Commit ladder & MAP for VPC pilot — technical & licensing notes

Maya — quick engineering note from our side that affects acceptance gates:

- For Private/VPC deployments we'll need a short maintenance window for kernel-level optimizations (estimated 2–4 hours) during pilot onboarding. We'll coordinate with your infra team.
- If you plan to enable heavy quantized models for cost reasons, licensing differs for mixed-precision vs custom-kernel builds; that impacts unit price tiers in the MAP.

On licensing: we recommend adding a clause that allows a one-time conversion of pilot usage to committed units (with a waterfall discount schedule) to avoid double-billing during the ramp. I'll flag exact language for the SOW redline.

—Karthik
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 11:05 AM Sofia Ivanova wrote:
> Maya — thanks for the checklist and the timetable. I've put together a draft MAP...

From: Maya Rao <maya@acmecorp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com, pete.harris@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-11-13T10:40:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Commit ladder & MAP for VPC pilot — feedback and redlines

Sofia / team — thank you for the fast turnaround. Procurement reviewed the MAP and SRE reviewed the technical tasks. A couple of redlines / asks:

- Platform fee amortization: Procurement prefers a fixed amortization schedule rather than a conditional credit. Proposed: platform fee amortized evenly across the first 12 months of the commit with a 60-day rollback window if the GA gate is missed.
- Acceptance criteria: we need specific throughput targets for the 30/60-day gates (p95 < 150ms on our internally simulated traffic). Please add them to the MAP or SOW.
- Escrow / audit: Procurement asks for SOC2 evidence + quarterly access to audit logs for the pilot.

We're fine with a DocuSign path if the SOW redline contains firm dates and the amortization schedule. Can you provide a redline SOW by Monday?

—Maya
Head of Cloud Engineering, Acme Corporation

Attachments: redline_acme_comments.pdf (commented PDF, 78KB)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Updated MAP + redline SOW (commercial ladder & amortization)

Maya — attached are the updated materials: redline_SOW-draft.docx (incorporates throughput targets and an amortization table) and an updated MAP that implements a fixed 12-month amortization with a 60-day rollback clause as requested. Highlights: 

- 30-day gate: performance baseline collection (p95 < 150ms), SOC2 evidence snapshot for pilot scope.
- 60-day gate: throughput test (sustained X RPS) + security validation. Passing 60-day gate triggers 30% committed capacity at tier-1 unit price.
- GA ramp: 12-month staircase commit with 4 ramp steps (25% increments). Platform fee amortized evenly across the 12 months; if ramp misses 50% of committed usage by 90 days, a one-time adjustment credit is applied per the table in the SOW.

I've pushed the redline to HubSpot and created a DocuSign envelope for the MSA redline so Procurement can route signatures quickly: https://docusign.example/sign/ACME-MSA-2026 and HubSpot link: https://hubspot.example/contacts/ACME-72

Requested next steps:
- Procurement to confirm the 60-day rollback window and amortization table by EOD Friday.
- Engineering (Acme) to provide an initial simulated traffic profile for our SRE team so we can validate the p95 target.
- If accepted, we'll send a final commercial summary for signature.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_SOW-draft.docx (word doc, 98KB), MAP-railmap-v2.pdf (diagram, 125KB)

Related: HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/contacts/ACME-72, DocuSign: https://docusign.example/sign/ACME-MSA-2026

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@acmecorp.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Updated MAP + redline SOW — SRE confirmation and pricing ask

Maya — quick note from SRE & solutions: the acceptance gates and amortization schedule look implementable. Two asks before commercial sign:

1) Finalized ramp numbers (committed units by month) so we can size autoscale and reserve capacity — if you can share a 3-month ramp spreadsheet we will produce a cost-curve.
2) Confirm whether mixed-precision models will be in scope for the pilot (affects kernel licensing line-item).

If Procurement can sign the MSA redline in DocuSign and share the ramp spreadsheet, we will prepare a final commercial summary for signature. Happy to review the TCO model together next week.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
diego@redwoodinference.com
